body:
Validates `shell` (default `pwsh`) is executable before building
`cmd`; returns nil and logs instead of spawning a broken process.

Resolves the PowerShellEditorServices module path via
`Get-Module -ListAvailable` when `bundle_path` is unset.

Defaults `init_options.enableProfileLoading` to `false`, since a
profile that writes to stdout corrupts the LSP handshake. Override
via `init_options` if needed.

Requires neovim/neovim#41479, which makes `Client.create` return
`nil, err` instead of erroring when `cmd()` returns nil.

> Hey,
> 
> I am not sure if this is the right place to write that, but there was a change in this pull request, which breaks the start of the lsp server for powershell_es as the `command_fmt` variable was altered.
> 
The old format was wrong, the lsp did not start at all with it. There is a contradiction in the command. The `-BundledModulesPath '%s'` part requires the actual module path, not the root folder, and the `'%s/PowerShellEditorServices/Start-EditorServices.ps1'` part requires the root folder.
I tested with both autodetection and manual override using setup. The example in the comments of the file:
```
vim.lsp.config('powershell_es', {
  bundle_path = 'c:/w/PowerShellEditorServices',
})
```
The old format yields 'c:/w/PowerShellEditorServices/PowerShellEditorServices/Start-EditorServices.ps1', this path does not exist, the lsp does not start because of this.

> The old format was wrong, the lsp did not start at all with it.

Works for me.

> There is a contradiction in the command. The -BundledModulesPath '%s' part requires the actual module path, not the root folder

As per https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShellEditorServices#advanced-usage
`-BundledModulesPath` is the parent of `PowerShellEditorServices/` folder, namely the root folder.

The name `-BundledModulesPath` implies the folder given should include more than one modules, i.e. `PowerShellEditorServices`, `PSReadline` and `PSScriptAnalyzer`, not the individual `PowerShellEditorServices`.

> > The old format was wrong, the lsp did not start at all with it.
> 
> Works for me.
> 
> > There is a contradiction in the command. The -BundledModulesPath '%s' part requires the actual module path, not the root folder
> 
> As per https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShellEditorServices#advanced-usage `-BundledModulesPath` is the parent of `PowerShellEditorServices/` folder, namely the root folder.
> 
> The name `-BundledModulesPath` implies the folder given should include more than one modules, i.e. `PowerShellEditorServices`, `PSReadline` and `PSScriptAnalyzer`, not the individual `PowerShellEditorServices`.

You have a point here, BundledModulesPath points to other modules, but definitely not to PowerShellEditorServices, it cannot point to itself - this is redundant. Customary the other modules are bundled with PowerShellEditorServices in the same folder, but they don't have to be.
It was my misunderstanding of this parameter. I will open a PR to fix this.

I checked C# code https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShellEditorServices/blob/ba8b42071c097536d240e857b2b1cf3dcd1e1fbc/src/PowerShellEditorServices.Hosting/Commands/StartEditorServicesCommand.cs

`BundledModulesPath` default value is 3 branches up the tree from the assemly:

```
[Parameter]
[ValidateNotNullOrEmpty]
public string BundledModulesPath { get; set; } = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(
    Path.GetDirectoryName(typeof(StartEditorServicesCommand).Assembly.Location),
    "..", "..", ".."));
```
The location of the assembly in the main.zip package is

`PowerShellEditorServices\bin\Core\Microsoft.PowerShell.EditorServices.Hosting.dll`

It translates to the parent folder of PowerShellEditorServices folder.

Since `powershell_es.lua` did the same thing in the prior version:
```
[[& '%s/PowerShellEditorServices/Start-EditorServices.ps1' -BundledModulesPath '%s' -LogPath '%s/powershell_es.log' -SessionDetailsPath '%s/powershell_es.session.json' -FeatureFlags @() -AdditionalModules @() -HostName nvim -HostProfileId 0 -HostVersion 1.0.0 -Stdio -LogLevel Normal]]
```
It is redundant to include it at all. I am not sure why the argument `-BundledModulesPath '%s'` was even included if there were no option to change it. I suggest to change the command to the following:
```
[[& '%s/PowerShellEditorServices/Start-EditorServices.ps1' -LogPath '%s/powershell_es.log' -SessionDetailsPath '%s/powershell_es.session.json' -FeatureFlags @() -AdditionalModules @() -HostName nvim -HostProfileId 0 -HostVersion 1.0.0 -Stdio -LogLevel Normal]]
```
Does everyone agree with this?
No just don't, focus on what you intended in the first place. Simplifying command is unnecessary, neither a fix nor feature. Just push the fix
